# Consolidate rb_malloc/rb_free into src/rb_alloc.c

## Context

`src/rbtree.c` currently defines the plain `rb_malloc`/`rb_free` wrappers
inline (forwarding to `malloc`/`free`), and `tests/fault_malloc.c` defines
its own `rb_malloc`/`rb_free` (fault-injecting versions), with a comment
claiming these are "strong overrides of the weak rb_malloc/rb_free in
src/rbtree.c." That's not actually true — neither definition is marked
`__attribute__((weak))`. I confirmed this by running `make test`:

```
/bin/ld: multiple definition of `rb_malloc'; ... first defined here
/bin/ld: multiple definition of `rb_free'; ... first defined here
```

The build is currently broken. `$(BIN)` compiles `tests/test_rbtree.c`
(which `#include`s `src/rbtree.c` for white-box access) together with
`tests/fault_malloc.c` — so both real definitions land in one binary and
the linker rejects the duplicate symbols.

## Fix: move the plain wrappers to their own file, not into fault_malloc.c

Moving the plain wrappers out of `rbtree.c` into a new `src/rb_alloc.c`
resolves the conflict *without* needing to rename anything in
`fault_malloc.c`, because of how the Makefile already separates the two
binaries:

- `$(BIN)` (test binary) compiles only `$(TSRC)` = `test_rbtree.c` +
  `fault_malloc.c`. Once `rbtree.c` no longer defines `rb_malloc`/`rb_free`
  itself (just declares them), `fault_malloc.c`'s definitions become the
  *only* ones linked in — no conflict.
- `$(FUZZBIN)` compiles `$(SRC)` + `tests/fuzz.c`. Adding `src/rb_alloc.c`
  to `$(SRC)` supplies the plain wrappers there — `fault_malloc.c` is never
  linked into this binary, so again no conflict.

The two implementations are never linked together in any current target,
so no renaming is needed. This is the "preferably in src/" branch of the
request.

Because `include/rbtree.h` is the graded contract and can't be touched
(and it doesn't declare `rb_malloc`/`rb_free` anyway — they're internal),
a small internal header `src/rb_alloc.h` carries the prototypes so
`rbtree.c` has a visible declaration before calling them (required under
`-std=c23`, which errors on implicit declarations).

## Files

**New: `src/rb_alloc.h`**
```c
#ifndef RB_ALLOC_H
#define RB_ALLOC_H

#include <stddef.h>

void *rb_malloc(size_t size);
void rb_free(void *ptr);

#endif
```

**New: `src/rb_alloc.c`**
```c
#include "rb_alloc.h"

#include <stdlib.h>

void *rb_malloc(size_t size)
{
    return malloc(size);
}

void rb_free(void *ptr)
{
    free(ptr);
}
```

**Edit `src/rbtree.c`**: remove the inline `rb_malloc`/`rb_free`
definitions and the now-unused `<stdlib.h>` include; include
`"rb_alloc.h"` instead.
```c
#include "rbtree.h"
#include "rb_alloc.h"
#include <string.h>

typedef struct rbnode {
...
```

**Edit `tests/fault_malloc.c`**: include the new header (for a matching
prototype) and correct the stale "weak override" comment.
```c
#include "../src/rb_alloc.h"
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Definitions of rb_malloc/rb_free for the test binary. The Makefile links
 * this file instead of src/rb_alloc.c into $(BIN), so these are the only
 * rb_malloc/rb_free in that binary -- lets tests force a specific rb_malloc
 * call to fail without touching libc malloc or the production wrappers. */

static int fault_armed = 0;
... (unchanged below)
```

**Edit `Makefile`**: add the new file to `SRC` so `$(FUZZBIN)` picks it up,
and add `src/rb_alloc.h` as a prerequisite of both binaries (parallel to
the existing `include/rbtree.h` prerequisite).
```make
SRC := src/rbtree.c src/rb_alloc.c
TSRC := tests/test_rbtree.c tests/fault_malloc.c
BIN := build/test_rbtree
FUZZBIN := build/fuzz

$(BIN): $(SRC) $(TSRC) include/rbtree.h src/rb_alloc.h
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(TSRC) -o $@
$(FUZZBIN): $(SRC) tests/fuzz.c include/rbtree.h src/rb_alloc.h
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(SRC) tests/fuzz.c -o $@
```
(`$(BIN)`'s recipe still doesn't compile `$(SRC)` directly — same
double-definition reasoning as the existing comment above that target,
now doubly important since `src/rb_alloc.c` must stay out of `$(BIN)`.)

## Verification

Run `make test`, `make memcheck`, and `make asan` (per CLAUDE.md, expected
to fail from missing libraries as of 8/29 — show output anyway) and
confirm `make test` now links and the full suite passes.

# Consolidate rb_malloc/rb_free into src/rb_alloc.c

## Context

`src/rbtree.c` currently defines the plain `rb_malloc`/`rb_free` wrappers
inline (forwarding to `malloc`/`free`), and `tests/fault_malloc.c` defines
its own `rb_malloc`/`rb_free` (fault-injecting versions), with a comment
claiming these are "strong overrides of the weak rb_malloc/rb_free in
src/rbtree.c." That's not actually true — neither definition is marked
`__attribute__((weak))`. I confirmed this by running `make test`:

```
/bin/ld: multiple definition of `rb_malloc'; ... first defined here
/bin/ld: multiple definition of `rb_free'; ... first defined here
```

The build is currently broken. `$(BIN)` compiles `tests/test_rbtree.c`
(which `#include`s `src/rbtree.c` for white-box access) together with
`tests/fault_malloc.c` — so both real definitions land in one binary and
the linker rejects the duplicate symbols.

## Fix: move the plain wrappers to their own file, not into fault_malloc.c

Moving the plain wrappers out of `rbtree.c` into a new `src/rb_alloc.c`
resolves the conflict *without* needing to rename anything in
`fault_malloc.c`, because of how the Makefile already separates the two
binaries:

- `$(BIN)` (test binary) compiles only `$(TSRC)` = `test_rbtree.c` +
  `fault_malloc.c`. Once `rbtree.c` no longer defines `rb_malloc`/`rb_free`
  itself (just declares them), `fault_malloc.c`'s definitions become the
  *only* ones linked in — no conflict.
- `$(FUZZBIN)` compiles `$(SRC)` + `tests/fuzz.c`. Adding `src/rb_alloc.c`
  to `$(SRC)` supplies the plain wrappers there — `fault_malloc.c` is never
  linked into this binary, so again no conflict.

The two implementations are never linked together in any current target,
so no renaming is needed. This is the "preferably in src/" branch of the
request.

Because `include/rbtree.h` is the graded contract and can't be touched
(and it doesn't declare `rb_malloc`/`rb_free` anyway — they're internal),
a small internal header `src/rb_alloc.h` carries the prototypes so
`rbtree.c` has a visible declaration before calling them (required under
`-std=c23`, which errors on implicit declarations).

## Files

**New: `src/rb_alloc.h`**
```c
#ifndef RB_ALLOC_H
#define RB_ALLOC_H

#include <stddef.h>

void *rb_malloc(size_t size);
void rb_free(void *ptr);

#endif
```

**New: `src/rb_alloc.c`**
```c
#include "rb_alloc.h"

#include <stdlib.h>

void *rb_malloc(size_t size)
{
    return malloc(size);
}

void rb_free(void *ptr)
{
    free(ptr);
}
```

**Edit `src/rbtree.c`**: remove the inline `rb_malloc`/`rb_free`
definitions and the now-unused `<stdlib.h>` include; include
`"rb_alloc.h"` instead.
```c
#include "rbtree.h"
#include "rb_alloc.h"
#include <string.h>

typedef struct rbnode {
...
```

**Edit `tests/fault_malloc.c`**: include the new header (for a matching
prototype) and correct the stale "weak override" comment.
```c
#include "../src/rb_alloc.h"
#include <stdlib.h>

/* Definitions of rb_malloc/rb_free for the test binary. The Makefile links
 * this file instead of src/rb_alloc.c into $(BIN), so these are the only
 * rb_malloc/rb_free in that binary -- lets tests force a specific rb_malloc
 * call to fail without touching libc malloc or the production wrappers. */

static int fault_armed = 0;
... (unchanged below)
```

**Edit `Makefile`**: add the new file to `SRC` so `$(FUZZBIN)` picks it up,
and add `src/rb_alloc.h` as a prerequisite of both binaries (parallel to
the existing `include/rbtree.h` prerequisite).
```make
SRC := src/rbtree.c src/rb_alloc.c
TSRC := tests/test_rbtree.c tests/fault_malloc.c
BIN := build/test_rbtree
FUZZBIN := build/fuzz

$(BIN): $(SRC) $(TSRC) include/rbtree.h src/rb_alloc.h
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(TSRC) -o $@
$(FUZZBIN): $(SRC) tests/fuzz.c include/rbtree.h src/rb_alloc.h
	@mkdir -p build
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) $(SRC) tests/fuzz.c -o $@
```
(`$(BIN)`'s recipe still doesn't compile `$(SRC)` directly — same
double-definition reasoning as the existing comment above that target,
now doubly important since `src/rb_alloc.c` must stay out of `$(BIN)`.)

## Verification

Run `make test`, `make memcheck`, and `make asan` (per CLAUDE.md, expected
to fail from missing libraries as of 8/29 — show output anyway) and
confirm `make test` now links and the full suite passes.
